findings.issue: The selected, image-checked edition prints a period between the article τῶν and its noun νεκρῶν. The English defensibly reads them together, but the notes do not disclose this anomalous printed punctuation. It should not be silently treated as an OCR error.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted editorial note recording the supplied reading “τῶν. νεκρῶν.” and explaining that the English reads the article and noun together despite the intervening printed period. Distinguish any proposed removal of that period from the selected edition's actual reading. The supplied print verification makes this a disclosure issue, not a reason to require renewed source verification.

findings.source_quote: ἀπὸ τοῦ μὴ θέλοντος, συναπολέσθαι δὲ βουλομένου;
findings.english_quote: from the one who does not want this but wishes them to perish together?
findings.issue: The understood subject of συναπολέσθαι is the person described by βουλομένου: that person wishes to perish together with another. “Wishes them to perish together” instead supplies a third-person plural subject and can make this a wish for other people's destruction without retaining the unwilling person's own co-perishing. “This” also leaves the object of the preceding refusal less clear than the Greek's parallel with wanting to be saved.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “from the one who does not want to be saved but wants to perish together?” Alternatively, “wants to perish along with the other” makes the contextual companion explicit. Preserve the unwilling person as the subject of the desired co-perishing. Any replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὅθεν οἱ ἀπειθεῖς ἐπακούειν αὐτῶν μὴ θέλοντες αὐτοὶ αὐτοὺς ἐπολέμουν, χωρίζοντες, διώκοντες, μισοῦντες.
findings.english_quote: Therefore the disobedient, unwilling to listen to them, themselves fought against them, separating from them, persecuting them, and hating them.
findings.issue: “Separating from them” takes active χωρίζοντες intransitively, as the disobedient people's withdrawal. In the parallel sequence, αὐτούς can instead supply the object of χωρίζοντες as well as διώκοντες and μισοῦντες: the disobedient impose separation on those who did not want to separate. This materially different account of agency is not disclosed in the notes.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the more source-transparent wording “themselves fought against them, separating them, persecuting them, and hating them.” If retaining the intransitive rendering, document the shared-object alternative and explain the contextual reason for choosing withdrawal rather than imposed separation. Review the resulting wording and note anew.
